description: Native OpenAI-compatible adapters: OpenAI (P2.4), LM Studio + generic OpenAI-compatible (P2.5), and Azure OpenAI (P2.6). All three reuse the shared HTTP/SSE client from capability.rs and the ChatProvider contract from FEAT-001. They share one native code path; only base_url/headers/path-rewriting differ. Depends on FEAT-001. Adapters are independent of the FEAT-003 shims. Tests use mocked HTTP + SSE fixtures only (no live network); compile/test/clippy of the providers crate are DEFERRED TO CI (offline sandbox cannot reach crates.io).
steps: Implement P2.4 in crates/providers/src/adapters/openai.rs: a ChatProvider impl that maps the internal OpenAI-compatible ChatRequest straight through to POST {base_url}/chat/completions with `Authorization: Bearer <key>` (key resolved via SecretStore at call time, never stored). base_url default https://api.openai.com/v1. Implement both chat (non-streaming: parse ChatResponse) and chat_stream (SSE deltas -> ChatDelta via the shared client, terminating on [DONE]). Implement list_models (GET {base_url}/models -> Vec<ModelInfo>) and capabilities(model) returning sensible per-model defaults (streaming+tools true; vision/json_mode/max_context best-effort). Build the struct from ProviderConfig via a ProviderFactory for ProviderKind::OpenAI.

Implement P2.5 LM Studio in crates/providers/src/adapters/lmstudio.rs: reuse the SAME native code path as OpenAI (Section 4.3 - deliberately identical, only base_url differs). base_url default http://localhost:1234/v1, NO api key by default (do not send Authorization when api_key_ref is None). Provide a ProviderFactory for ProviderKind::LmStudio. Factor the shared native adapter logic so OpenAI/LM Studio/Generic reuse one implementation parameterized by base_url + auth strategy rather than duplicating request/stream code.

Implement the generic OpenAI-compatible path in crates/providers/src/adapters/generic_openai.rs for ProviderKind::GenericOpenAI: same native code path, base_url is user-supplied (required; error clearly if missing), optional Bearer key. Provide its ProviderFactory. This is the escape hatch for any user-supplied OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

Implement P2.6 Azure OpenAI in crates/providers/src/adapters/azure_openai.rs for ProviderKind::Azure (near-direct): base_url = resource endpoint; rewrite request path to /openai/deployments/{deployment}/chat/completions; add `api-version` query param and `api-key` header (NOT Bearer); read extra.deployment and extra.api_version from ProviderConfig.extra (error clearly if deployment/api_version missing). Reuse the shared HTTP/SSE client for both streaming and non-streaming. Provide its ProviderFactory.

Add unit/integration tests (in each adapter module and/or providers/tests/) using a mocked HTTP server (wiremock or httpmock) that returns RECORDED/fixture OpenAI chat completion JSON (non-streaming) and a fixture SSE body (`data: {chunk}` frames + `data: [DONE]`) for streaming. Assert: (a) request translation - correct method/path/headers/body for each adapter (OpenAI Bearer; LM Studio no auth; Azure path-rewrite + api-key header + api-version query + reads extra.deployment/api_version); (b) stream normalization - SSE frames decode into ordered ChatDelta values and the stream terminates on [DONE]; (c) non-streaming parses into ChatResponse; (d) capability negotiation gates behavior (e.g. a model reporting tools=false causes tools to be omitted from the outbound body). Point the mock server URL as base_url so NO live network is used.

Document (as a #[ignore]d test or a doc comment in lmstudio.rs) the OPTIONAL manual LM Studio integration check against a real http://localhost:1234/v1 returning a streamed completion - explicitly NOT run in CI (Section 4.3 / tasks.md acceptance).

Update crates/providers/src/lib.rs adapters module exports as needed; remove any now-satisfied #[allow(dead_code)] placeholders for these adapters. Run `cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/providers/Cargo.toml`. Re-run offline `cargo build/test/clippy --workspace` to confirm offline members remain green (providers itself compiles only in CI).
acceptance_criteria: openai.rs, lmstudio.rs, generic_openai.rs, azure_openai.rs each provide a ChatProvider impl and a ProviderFactory for their ProviderKind, sharing one native code path parameterized by base_url + auth.

OpenAI uses Bearer auth vs https://api.openai.com/v1; LM Studio defaults to http://localhost:1234/v1 with no key; Generic requires a user base_url; Azure rewrites to /openai/deployments/{deployment}/chat/completions with api-version query + api-key header reading extra.deployment/api_version.
Mocked-HTTP tests assert request translation and SSE stream normalization for each adapter, using fixtures and a mock server URL (no live network).
A capability-negotiation test proves tools/streaming are gated per Capabilities.
An #[ignore]d/documented manual LM Studio localhost integration test exists and is not run in CI.
Offline `cargo build/test/clippy --workspace` remain green; `cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/providers/Cargo.toml --check` clean.
verification: From hybrid-orchestrator/: `cargo build --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (offline members)
Review confirms adapter tests use mocked HTTP/SSE fixtures and share the native code path; providers crate compile/test/clippy deferred to CI.
findings:
Implemented all four native OpenAI-compatible adapters over a single shared code path in a new module crates/providers/src/adapters/native.rs (NativeAdapter). NativeAdapter is parameterized by (a) base_url via HttpSseClient, (b) an AuthStrategy enum {None, Bearer(key), ApiKeyHeader(key)}, and (c) a Routing enum {Standard, Azure{deployment, api_version}}. It implements ChatProvider: chat (non-streaming, post_json -> ChatResponse), chat_stream (post_sse with a parse_stream_chunk fn that flattens OpenAI `choices[0].delta` chunks into ChatDelta, skipping role-only openers, terminating on [DONE] via the FEAT-001 sse decoder), list_models (GET /models -> Vec<ModelInfo>), and capabilities (per-provider defaults: streaming+tools+json_mode true, vision false, max_context None). The outbound body forces the `stream` flag and splices ChatRequest.extra members to the top level (extra is an internal-only container, not an OpenAI field).

The four thin adapter modules each expose a build_* fn + a ProviderFactory: openai.rs (OpenAiFactory, ProviderKind::OpenAI, Bearer, default base https://api.openai.com/v1, requires api_key_ref -> Auth error if missing); lmstudio.rs (LmStudioFactory, ProviderKind::LmStudio, default base http://localhost:1234/v1, AuthStrategy::None when api_key_ref is None so NO Authorization header is sent, Bearer if a key is configured); generic_openai.rs (GenericOpenAiFactory, ProviderKind::GenericOpenAI, base_url REQUIRED -> clear Other error if missing/empty, optional Bearer); azure_openai.rs (AzureOpenAiFactory, ProviderKind::Azure, reads extra.deployment + extra.api_version -> clear Other errors if missing, rewrites path to /openai/deployments/{deployment}/chat/completions with ?api-version=... and uses the `api-key` header, NOT Bearer). Factories re-exported from lib.rs; adapters module reorganized (native + four impls active; anthropic/gemini/bedrock remain FEAT-003 stubs, untouched).

Added HttpSseClient::get_json to capability.rs (the shared client previously only did POST) so list_models can GET /models through the same client.

Tests: unit tests in native.rs (body splicing/stream flag, all three auth header strategies, Standard vs Azure routing paths, stream-chunk flattening incl. tool_calls + finish_reason + role-only skip); per-module error-path tests in generic_openai.rs and azure_openai.rs (missing base_url/deployment/api_version/key). Integration tests in crates/providers/tests/adapters.rs use wiremock (dev-dep already present) pointing base_url at the mock server (NO live network): OpenAI Bearer + non-streaming decode + GET /models + body translation (body_partial_json) + SSE stream normalization into ordered deltas terminating on [DONE]; LM Studio asserts NO Authorization header (via a respond_with closure inspecting the captured request); Generic asserts user base_url + Bearer; Azure asserts path-rewrite + api-version query_param + api-key header; and a capability-negotiation test proving negotiate() strips tools (tools=false) before the request goes out (mock asserts the outbound body has no `tools` key). An #[ignore]d manual LM Studio localhost integration test (tests::manual_lmstudio_localhost_stream) is documented in lmstudio.rs and excluded from CI.

Verified OFFLINE from hybrid-orchestrator/: `cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/providers/Cargo.toml --check` clean; `cargo build --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` all green (these cover only the offline members mcp-client + routing; providers stays under [workspace] exclude). DEFERRED TO CI (INTEGRATIONS_ONLY sandbox: crates.io 403, so the providers crate cannot compile locally): the actual compile/clippy/test of the providers crate run in CI via the existing `--manifest-path crates/providers/Cargo.toml` steps FEAT-001 added to .github/workflows/ci.yml (no CI changes needed for FEAT-002). No source files other than the providers crate were modified. wiremock 0.6 API assumptions (body_partial_json matcher, Fn(&Request)->ResponseTemplate Respond impl, Request.headers as http::HeaderMap, Request.body as Vec<u8>) are validated only in CI.
